ap_computer_science_a-m15.stem: Which of the following is the weakest precondition (the least restrictive condition) that guarantees the method slice will not throw an exception?

options.text: len is at most s.length() and start is any int value.
options.why: This does not prevent start + len from passing the end, as slice("hello", 3, 4) shows.

options.text: start + len is less than s.length() and neither start nor len is negative.
options.why: This is stronger than needed (start + len may equal s.length()), although it does exclude negative values of start and len.

options.text: start is at least 0, len is at least 0, and start + len is at most s.length().
options.why: substring needs 0 <= start and start + len <= s.length(), and a negative len makes the end index smaller than start.

options.text: start is at least 0, and len is greater than 0 and at most s.length().
options.why: This is stronger than needed and also incomplete: it does not stop start + len from exceeding s.length().
